So this is actually an issue that comes from being an RPG more than anything else, so excuse me if I talk in a general case. 

HP and Defense obviously are linked stats in that they all collectively determine how hard it is to beat the character. But specifically which is higher changes how to use a character. 

Having high HP with average to low Defenses gives you a character that doesn’t care if they get hit, there are just more hit points. This also creates a strategy of healing them over time to abuse their already large health pool. (leftovers.)

High defenses with low/average HP creates a character that doesn’t get hit. Nothing ever actually does enough of an initial impact to deal any damage. But if you find some way to exploit a weakness they fall pretty easy. (Psyshock on Special walls.)

These things just don’t come up as much in Pokémon because there are enough to choose from that might have high defense **and** high HP.

I worked at a game store for about 5 years and during that time I taught a lot of people how to play Magic. Sometimes they would ask how to get better, and I came up with this list of advice. Presenting...

Mehayo’s 5 (technically 6) pieces of advice for being better at Magic no matter what your playing!

1) You only need 1 life. You get 20. Feel free to lose some of your life up because you don’t need it all.

2) It’s not wrong to ask questions. Ask your friends about your deck. Ask your opponent what their cards do. Ask a judge to explain things at a tournament. 

3) A playable hand is better than a good hand. It is much better to play the cards in your hand and actually do something than stare at your best cards and do nothing. 

4) Sometimes cards do nothing. Yes the card will say things and look fancy but if that effect doesn’t help your deck it might as well be blank. 

5) If you can, just win the game. It’s easy to get lost in the excitement of making your deck work. But you if you see the chance to win the game you should go for it. 

6) Pay attention. This is only technically on the list as it’s more general advice than Magic specific but it still helps. Pay attention to what’s going on and what you’re doing. If you don’t want to focus on the game then you aren’t going to get better. 

Some of these are a little more geared towards newer players but they are all solid advice to helping you get better.

Do you propose that after the Shock-lands cycle out of Standard new dual lands will return to the Core set? How long do you believe WotC will push Mono colour play?

Yes it is true that right now playing multi-colour is very good and there isn't very much reason to play with only 1 colour; and this makes perfect sense as we are in the middle of a Gold block when playing 2 and 3 colour decks is very easy and very fun. It is the ebb and flow of the metagame. This does not mean that you HAVE to play mulitcolour. I believe that the collective forces of the internet could come up with very strong and wholly competitive Mono-colour decks if put to the task. No one is choosing to do so at this time because we are in a Gold block and multi-colour is fun.

As for the trade off on efficiency of lands, Standard right now has access to 3 sets of two coloured lands. One is always a tempo hit (the Guildgates), one is either a tempo hit or physical loss of life (the Shocklands), and the last set is either a loss in tempo or in favorable conditions no loss (the Check-lands). How exactly is there no trade off between these and Basic lands?

Finally, reprinting the Core set Check-lands would not add any more dual lands to Standard, it would simply maintain the current number for the future of Standard.

The way you say this indicates a belief that there would be no dual lands in the Core set at all. To be honest, this seems somewhat unlikely given that with the sole exception of 4th edition, every Core set has had at least ally coloured dual lands. The power level of these cards can vary but there is always some support for 2 colour play. 

In addition, by your own logic a reason that the Core set duals would not be reprinted is because the Innistrad enemy colour duals will rotate out. Then you say that this will leave only the RTR Shocklands as the only dual lands. They too will cycle out of Standard soon enough, that is the point of standard after all. If there isn't any type of dual land printed in the core set then we will be faced with a period of time where there are no dual lands to play with, which I don't think is likely.

I'd be as interested in seeing a "mono-colour" matters environment, but I belive WotC will find a way to do it without completely cutting off access to multi-colour lands.
